questions.solution: A sentinel value ends the loop.

blocks.text:
for (int i = 1; i <= 4; i++)

questions.solution: The loop displays 2, 4, 6 and 8 without spaces.

questions.solution: Debugging is an activity, not a programming paradigm.

questions.solution: word[3] is 't' because array indexing starts at zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following are selection structures?
questions.solution: if and switch select among alternatives.

questions.stem: Which term describes a finite sequence of precise steps that solves a problem?
questions.solution: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of unambiguous steps.

questions.stem: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.solution: do...while tests the condition after the body.

questions.stem: Which identifier is valid in C++?
questions.solution: An identifier may contain letters, digits and underscores, but cannot start with a digit or be a keyword.

questions.stem: Which of the following declarations are valid?
questions.solution: a and c are valid array declarations.

questions.stem: Which values can a bool variable hold?
questions.solution: A bool holds true or false.

questions.stem: This question tests algorithms and programming errors.

parts.answer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of precise steps that solves a problem. Pseudocode is a structured English-like description of an algorithm.
parts.solution: Award 1 mark for each correct definition.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Explain THREE types of programming errors and give one example of each.
parts.answer: Syntax error: missing semicolon. Runtime error: division by zero. Logic error: using < instead of <= in a condition.
parts.solution: Award 0.5 mark for each type and 0.5 mark for a valid example.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A program reads a student's score from 0 to 100 and displays the grade shown in Table 1.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the grade classification.
parts.answer: Start -> read score -> decision score >= 80 -> A; else score >= 60 -> B; else score >= 50 -> C; else score >= 40 -> D; else F -> display grade -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for terminal symbols, input, four/five decisions, each output and correct flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode for the algorithm and convert it into a complete C++ program.
parts.answer: IF score >= 80 THEN grade = A ELSE IF score >= 60 THEN grade = B ... ENDIF; use if/else if in C++ and display grade.
parts.solution: Award marks for correct pseudocode, complete C++ structure, conditions, input and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests declarations, constants and expressions.

parts.text: Write C++ declarations for: an integer age, a double price, a constant discount rate of 0.10 and a character grade.
parts.answer: int age; double price; const double DISCOUNT = 0.10; char grade;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct types, names and const initialisation.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write C++ statements to read age and price, calculate price after discount, and display the result.
parts.answer: cin >> age >> price; price = price - price * DISCOUNT; cout << price;
parts.solution: Award marks for input, discount expression and output.
parts.label: b

parts.text: Trace the program and show the exact output.
parts.solution: Award marks for each line and the exact row lengths.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Identify TWO logic errors in a version that prints four rows but reuses j without resetting it. Rewrite the corrected code.
parts.answer: The inner loop must initialise j = 1 for every row and the outer loop must run to 4. Correct code: for (int i=1;i<=4;i++){for(int j=1;j<=i;j++) cout<<j; cout<<endl;}
parts.solution: Award marks for each error and the corrected loop.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A shop stores the item prices shown in Table 1.

parts.text: Declare an array named prices using the values in Table 1. Display all values.
parts.answer: double prices[5] = {20.5, 55.0, 15.9, 75.0, 10.0}; for (int i=0;i<5;i++) cout << prices[i] << endl;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct type, initialiser, loop and output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment that applies a 10% discount to prices above RM50 and stores the results in a second array. Display both arrays.
parts.answer: double sale[5]; for(int i=0;i<5;i++){ sale[i] = prices[i] > 50 ? prices[i]*0.9 : prices[i]; } then display both arrays.
parts.solution: Award marks for second array, condition, discount, preservation and output.
parts.label: b
